chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubyd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, all from Safwan, or he said, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) had me read a sheet of the Book of Obligations (inheritance shares), which was dictated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and written by Ali (peace be upon him) with his own hand. So I found therein: a man who left his daughter and his mother. For the daughter is the half, three shares, and for the mother is the sixth, one share. The wealth is divided upon four shares. So whatever comes to three shares, it is for the daughter, and whatever comes to one share, it is for the mother.

He said, 'And I read in it: a man who left his daughter and his father. So for the daughter is the half, three shares, and for the father is the sixth, one share. The wealth is divided upon four shares. So whatever comes to three shares, it is for the daughter, and whatever comes to one share, it is for the mother.'

Muhammad said, 'And I found in it: a man who left his two parents and a daughter. So for the daughter is the half, three shares, and for the two parents, for each one of them, is the sixth, (one share for each of the two). The wealth is divided upon five shares. So whatever comes to three shares, it is for the daughter, and whatever comes to two shares, it is for the two parents.'
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance shares for a daughter and her parents according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the 'Sahifa' (a written document of inheritance rules) transmitted through Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, linking the practical application of fixed shares directly to the Prophet and Imam Ali. It clarifies the distribution logic where the daughter receives half (three shares) and the parents receive the sixth (one or two shares), demonstrating the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of prophetic knowledge in legal matters. The text serves as a foundational proof for the specific allocation of the 'residuary' portion to parents when a daughter is present, a key topic in Usul al-Fiqh.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubyd, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, altogether from Safwan, or he said, from Umar Bin Azina, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> made me read a book of the Obligations (legislated shares of inheritance) which was dictated by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and in the handwriting of Ali<sup>asws</sup> by his<sup>asws</sup> own hand. So I found therein a man who left his daughter, and his mother. For the daughter is the half, three shares, and for the mother is the six of the share. The wealth would be divided upon four shares. So what comes to three shares, so it is for the daughter, and whatever comes to one share so it is for the mother’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I read in it, a man who left his daughter and his father. So for the daughter is the half, three shares, and for the father is the sixth. The wealth is divided upon four shares. So whatever comes to three shares, so it is for the daughter, and whatever comes to one share, so it is for the mother’.

Muhammad (the narrator) said, ‘And I found in it, a man who left his two parents, and a daughter. So for the daughter is the half, three shares, and for the two parents, for each one of the two, is the sixth, (one share for each of the two of them). The wealth is divided upon five shares. So whatever comes three shares, so it is for the daughter, and whatever comes to two shares, so it is for the two parents’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al- Rahman all from Safwan or he said from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “Once abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, made me read the page of the book of ordained shares. It was according to the dictation of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and with the handwriting of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. I found in it this, ’If a deceased leaves behind his daughter and mother, the share of the daughter is one- half or three shares and for the mother one-sixth. The legacy is made in four parts, of which three are for the daughter and one is for the mother/”

“He (the narrator) has said, I read in it that, “If a deceased leaves behind his daughter and his father, the share of the daughter is one-half: three shares and the share of the father is one-sixth share. The legacy is made in four parts of which three are for the daughter and one is for the father.’”

“Muhammad has said, T found in it that if a deceased leaves behind both parents and his daughter; the share of the daughter is one-half, three shares and the shares of parents are one-sixth for each. Such legacy can be made of five portions of which three are for the daughter and two for the parents.’”
